items.title: Dawoud Sabu Adeyola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 30, 2025
items.q: my very first jazz concert ever that I went to was at Kleinhans Music Hall, which was the Cannonball Adderley Sextet with Nancy Wilson.

ctx.x: All right. I used to live in Buffalo myself for a while, and would go down to the Tralfamadore down those stairs, and I was thinking this morning, did the music scene, the jazz scene, which I know a lot of jazz musicians would pass through Buffalo. Did it make an impression on you when you were in your teenage years?

Oh without a doubt. Yeah. When I grew up here in Buffalo, first of all thanks for having me, I really appreciate this opportunity. I think it’s very important. As you know I’m a bit of a historian myself. I’ve written at least one book about the history of the Colored Musicians Club here in Buffalo, and its parent, Local 533. And there’s a new edition that should be forthcoming soon, which is kind of updating, you know, and, you know got a little bit more research materials in it. But yeah, when I grew up in…
Oh no. You just said the magic words.
